MAS1.AGENT_POPULATION_AND_SYSTEM_BOUNDARY: Candidate system includes autonomous decision loci and the environment they affect; a service collection is not assumed to be a MAS merely because it is distributed.
MAS1.GOAL_ALIGNMENT_AND_INCENTIVE_ASSUMPTIONS: Classify common-purpose, mixed-motive and competitive participation before importing cooperation or utility assumptions.
MAS1.INFORMATION_AND_CONTROL_DISTRIBUTION: Identify who knows each relevant fact, controls each action and bears consequences; physical distribution does not imply equal authority.
MAS1.COMMUNICATION_AND_PROTOCOL_SEMANTICS: Specify which dependencies require messages and whether a fixed direct interface suffices; natural language is optional.
MAS1.TASK_COMMITMENT_OR_RESOURCE_INTERDEPENDE: Decomposition is justified by genuine capability, information, resource, ownership or strategic interdependence, not agent count.
MAS1.ORGANISATIONAL_AUTHORITY_AND_NORMS: Authority may remain central even where observation and execution are distributed; rights are separate from technical access.
MAS1.GLOBAL_PROPERTY_AND_LOCAL_COMPOSITION: Assess the collective task, not an aggregate of unrelated local successes; compare alternative decompositions.
MAS1.DYNAMIC_MEMBERSHIP_LEARNING_AND_NONSTATI: Changing population or capabilities can invalidate a once-useful partition and require reassessment.
MAS1.FAILURE_DECEPTION_AND_COMMON_MODE_ASSUMP: Common models, data, networks and controllers remain correlated failure sources after decomposition.
MAS1.COLLECTIVE_EVALUATION_AND_COORDINATION_C: Comparator includes one capable agent, a scheduler and deterministic distributed services, matched to the same work and information.

MAS2.AGENT_POPULATION_AND_SYSTEM_BOUNDARY: Communicating participants may be heterogeneous and internally opaque; observers see message histories, not private beliefs.
MAS2.GOAL_ALIGNMENT_AND_INCENTIVE_ASSUMPTIONS: Message sincerity and protocol compliance are assumptions or separately evidenced behaviours, never consequences of a performative name.
MAS2.INFORMATION_AND_CONTROL_DISTRIBUTION: Each party has a local observation sequence; an omniscient shared transcript is not the default execution model.
MAS2.COMMUNICATION_AND_PROTOCOL_SEMANTICS: Separate transport, syntax, ontology, conversation identity, information causality and social effects; choose a stated semantic profile.
MAS2.TASK_COMMITMENT_OR_RESOURCE_INTERDEPENDE: A message may propose, create or report an obligation; none of these automatically performs the underlying task.
MAS2.ORGANISATIONAL_AUTHORITY_AND_NORMS: An institution or agreement determines who may create, release or delegate obligations; language syntax alone does not.
MAS2.GLOBAL_PROPERTY_AND_LOCAL_COMPOSITION: Local admissibility must be related to enactability, alignment or completion possibility under the selected semantics.
MAS2.DYNAMIC_MEMBERSHIP_LEARNING_AND_NONSTATI: Joining parties and changed ontologies need compatible interpretation and treatment of in-flight conversations.
MAS2.FAILURE_DECEPTION_AND_COMMON_MODE_ASSUMP: Delivery failure, duplicate or reordered messages, false reports and shared misunderstandings require distinct handling assumptions.
MAS2.COLLECTIVE_EVALUATION_AND_COORDINATION_C: Measure interoperability by correct consequential interaction; include translation, verification and conversation-state costs.

MAS3.AGENT_POPULATION_AND_SYSTEM_BOUNDARY: Workers, managers or peer allocators control tasks and resources; granularity may be dispatch-centre rather than vehicle or primitive action.
MAS3.GOAL_ALIGNMENT_AND_INCENTIVE_ASSUMPTIONS: Cooperative cost minimisation differs from privately profitable bidding; truthfulness is not supplied by an auction-shaped exchange.
MAS3.INFORMATION_AND_CONTROL_DISTRIBUTION: Capabilities, workloads and marginal task costs may be local; central scheduling is an admissible alternative when rights and information allow it.
MAS3.COMMUNICATION_AND_PROTOCOL_SEMANTICS: Announcements, bids, awards, withdrawals and completion reports need task correlation and agreed acceptance semantics.
MAS3.TASK_COMMITMENT_OR_RESOURCE_INTERDEPENDE: Task bundles, precedence, outstanding offers, deadlines and shared resources change feasible allocations and costs.
MAS3.ORGANISATIONAL_AUTHORITY_AND_NORMS: An award cannot grant permissions that the awarding party lacks; subcontracting and resource transfer have explicit limits.
MAS3.GLOBAL_PROPERTY_AND_LOCAL_COMPOSITION: Allocation quality and actual completed work are separate properties; local cost decreases need not resolve external resource conflicts.
MAS3.DYNAMIC_MEMBERSHIP_LEARNING_AND_NONSTATI: New tasks, departed workers and stale bids require expiry, reconsideration or replanning under an explicit responsibility model.
MAS3.FAILURE_DECEPTION_AND_COMMON_MODE_ASSUMP: Lost workers, deceptive bids and concurrent acceptance can strand or duplicate work; a shared allocator may itself fail.
MAS3.COLLECTIVE_EVALUATION_AND_COORDINATION_C: Count planning, negotiation, waiting and execution together; compare central or direct allocation and dependency elimination.

MAS4.AGENT_POPULATION_AND_SYSTEM_BOUNDARY: A team has identifiable participants and a joint activity; an observer grouping independent agents does not create membership commitments.
MAS4.GOAL_ALIGNMENT_AND_INCENTIVE_ASSUMPTIONS: Joint-intention and SharedPlans accounts normally presume cooperative commitments, with rules for legitimate reconsideration.
MAS4.INFORMATION_AND_CONTROL_DISTRIBUTION: Partial plans and local beliefs are permitted; what others must learn about changed circumstances is an explicit obligation.
MAS4.COMMUNICATION_AND_PROTOCOL_SEMANTICS: Team communication can notify achievement, impossibility, irrelevance, delegation or repair; some changes require recipients rather than broadcast.
MAS4.TASK_COMMITMENT_OR_RESOURCE_INTERDEPENDE: Intentions, public conditional commitments and actual performance are distinct objects that may be coupled but not equated.
MAS4.ORGANISATIONAL_AUTHORITY_AND_NORMS: Create, delegate, cancel and release have different actors; becoming aware of failure does not automatically authorise abandoning another party.
MAS4.GLOBAL_PROPERTY_AND_LOCAL_COMPOSITION: Collective persistence must coexist with achievable completion, repair and justified termination; local good intentions are insufficient.
MAS4.DYNAMIC_MEMBERSHIP_LEARNING_AND_NONSTATI: Goal changes and partner departures can trigger commitment reconsideration; continuation under obsolete assumptions can harm the team.
MAS4.FAILURE_DECEPTION_AND_COMMON_MODE_ASSUMP: Silent abandonment, stale commitment views and unverifiable completion remain possible outside the theory’s behavioural assumptions.
MAS4.COLLECTIVE_EVALUATION_AND_COORDINATION_C: Compare selective communication and partial planning with their cost; teamwork simulations do not establish all-domain superiority.

MAS5.AGENT_POPULATION_AND_SYSTEM_BOUNDARY: Strategic agents represent distinct decision makers, possibly with private values and outside options; a cooperative benchmark is a different population.
MAS5.GOAL_ALIGNMENT_AND_INCENTIVE_ASSUMPTIONS: State utility, rationality, equilibrium concept, information, transfers and participation assumptions; ethical value is not identical to utility.
MAS5.INFORMATION_AND_CONTROL_DISTRIBUTION: Types, bids and feasible allocations have specified visibility; an economic planner may be central without removing strategic interdependence.
MAS5.COMMUNICATION_AND_PROTOCOL_SEMANTICS: Bids and offers are strategic messages within a mechanism, not automatically accurate statements of need or cost.
MAS5.TASK_COMMITMENT_OR_RESOURCE_INTERDEPENDE: Allocation, payments, coalition formation and contract enforcement determine whether locally preferred actions support an objective.
MAS5.ORGANISATIONAL_AUTHORITY_AND_NORMS: Institutional permission and enforceable transfers must exist independently of equilibrium analysis; sanctions are not legitimate by optimisation alone.
MAS5.GLOBAL_PROPERTY_AND_LOCAL_COMPOSITION: Incentive compatibility, efficiency, individual rationality, budget balance and fairness are distinct, sometimes incompatible requirements.
MAS5.DYNAMIC_MEMBERSHIP_LEARNING_AND_NONSTATI: Entry, changing learning rules or a new opponent distribution can change equilibrium selection and stability.
MAS5.FAILURE_DECEPTION_AND_COMMON_MODE_ASSUMP: Collusion, non-modelled objectives, deception, incomplete computation and refusal to comply can defeat predicted behaviour.
MAS5.COLLECTIVE_EVALUATION_AND_COORDINATION_C: Evaluate welfare distribution, exploitability, solution-selection cost and computation; distinguish toy price games from real markets.

MAS6.AGENT_POPULATION_AND_SYSTEM_BOUNDARY: Organisations contain role players, organisational artefacts and possibly external human institutions; closed simulated institutions have narrower control.
MAS6.GOAL_ALIGNMENT_AND_INCENTIVE_ASSUMPTIONS: Agents may reason about norms or merely be constrained by infrastructure; compliance and shared goals are separate.
MAS6.INFORMATION_AND_CONTROL_DISTRIBUTION: Role specifications, local plans and institutional facts reside at different levels and need explicit access boundaries.
MAS6.COMMUNICATION_AND_PROTOCOL_SEMANTICS: Role adoption, mission acceptance, normative changes and violations have identifiable communicative or environmental evidence.
MAS6.TASK_COMMITMENT_OR_RESOURCE_INTERDEPENDE: Structural roles, functional goals and normative obligations must be linked where they jointly govern work.
MAS6.ORGANISATIONAL_AUTHORITY_AND_NORMS: Capability, permission, obligation, enforcement and external legitimacy are separate predicates; a plan’s violation option is not an ethical endorsement.
MAS6.GLOBAL_PROPERTY_AND_LOCAL_COMPOSITION: Permitted local transitions must be connected to organisational objectives and recovery, not only a well-formed role diagram.
MAS6.DYNAMIC_MEMBERSHIP_LEARNING_AND_NONSTATI: Reorganisation can change roles, missions or rules; existing obligations and affected participants constrain the transition.
MAS6.FAILURE_DECEPTION_AND_COMMON_MODE_ASSUMP: Off-platform acts, incomplete observation, norm conflict and self-serving monitors can defeat declared regulation.
MAS6.COLLECTIVE_EVALUATION_AND_COORDINATION_C: Assess compliance costs, lost flexibility, enforcement error and participation burden; prototypes are not proof of real institutional legitimacy.

MAS7.AGENT_POPULATION_AND_SYSTEM_BOUNDARY: Agents hold variables, constraints, arguments, preferences or observations; the object being aggregated must be stated before choosing an algorithm.
MAS7.GOAL_ALIGNMENT_AND_INCENTIVE_ASSUMPTIONS: DCOP commonly assumes cooperative objective evaluation; voting may instead face strategic preference reports.
MAS7.INFORMATION_AND_CONTROL_DISTRIBUTION: Variable ownership and graph structure determine information requirements; preserving local storage does not automatically preserve privacy.
MAS7.COMMUNICATION_AND_PROTOCOL_SEMANTICS: Constraint, utility, vote or argument messages have formally stated interpretations and transport assumptions.
MAS7.TASK_COMMITMENT_OR_RESOURCE_INTERDEPENDE: Coupled constraints and mutually attacking arguments create interdependence; factual corroboration additionally depends on evidence provenance.
MAS7.ORGANISATIONAL_AUTHORITY_AND_NORMS: A solution, acceptable extension or vote winner does not grant authority to implement it.
MAS7.GLOBAL_PROPERTY_AND_LOCAL_COMPOSITION: Completeness, optimality, acceptance and agreement refer to different models and should not be exchanged as guarantees.
MAS7.DYNAMIC_MEMBERSHIP_LEARNING_AND_NONSTATI: Changing constraints, participants or objectives invalidate static-model assurances unless the update mechanism is analysed.
MAS7.FAILURE_DECEPTION_AND_COMMON_MODE_ASSUMP: Incorrect utility messages, shared source errors, strategic votes and knowledge leakage are distinct threats.
MAS7.COLLECTIVE_EVALUATION_AND_COORDINATION_C: Include induced width, computation, bytes, disclosure and solution quality; algorithmic cycle counts are not end-to-end latency.

MAS8.AGENT_POPULATION_AND_SYSTEM_BOUNDARY: Learning populations may be fixed teams, competitive opponents or changing partners; state which agents and environment dynamics are adapted.
MAS8.GOAL_ALIGNMENT_AND_INCENTIVE_ASSUMPTIONS: Local reward, team return and social welfare need not coincide; a simulator’s reward is an authored objective.
MAS8.INFORMATION_AND_CONTROL_DISTRIBUTION: Centralised training may use joint state/actions unavailable to decentralised execution; this is an information contract, not a deployment privilege.
MAS8.COMMUNICATION_AND_PROTOCOL_SEMANTICS: Learned signalling or text communication must be tested for partner-compatible meaning and overhead, not assumed from fluency.
MAS8.TASK_COMMITMENT_OR_RESOURCE_INTERDEPENDE: Joint rewards, credit assignment and resource dependencies couple learning across agents and time.
MAS8.ORGANISATIONAL_AUTHORITY_AND_NORMS: A learning update can change behaviour but cannot itself confer permission to revise institutional rules.
MAS8.GLOBAL_PROPERTY_AND_LOCAL_COMPOSITION: Policy improvement, factorisation consistency and desirable emergence are different claims; test the collective trajectory.
MAS8.DYNAMIC_MEMBERSHIP_LEARNING_AND_NONSTATI: Other learners change the effective environment; cross-play and unseen-partner tests target failures hidden by self-play.
MAS8.FAILURE_DECEPTION_AND_COMMON_MODE_ASSUMP: Non-stationarity, correlated policies, exploitative equilibria and reward misspecification can produce collective failure.
MAS8.COLLECTIVE_EVALUATION_AND_COORDINATION_C: Evaluate seeds, tasks, partner populations, observation constraints and training cost; simulation-to-deployment transfer remains a separate claim.

MAS9.AGENT_POPULATION_AND_SYSTEM_BOUNDARY: Open populations may depart, be replaced, misbehave or share infrastructure; membership and identity assumptions are explicit.
MAS9.GOAL_ALIGNMENT_AND_INCENTIVE_ASSUMPTIONS: Accidental failure, rational defection and arbitrary malicious behaviour require different response models.
MAS9.INFORMATION_AND_CONTROL_DISTRIBUTION: Observers may suspect failure without knowing whether another agent is slow; recovery must account for hidden ongoing work.
MAS9.COMMUNICATION_AND_PROTOCOL_SEMANTICS: Failure notices, state reconciliation and retry messages require correlation; network partitions do not create new authority.
MAS9.TASK_COMMITMENT_OR_RESOURCE_INTERDEPENDE: Recovery handles outstanding tasks, commitments and resources, not merely restarting processes.
MAS9.ORGANISATIONAL_AUTHORITY_AND_NORMS: Reassignment and quarantine must stay within the designated parties’ powers; reputation is evidence for a bounded decision, not a universal licence.
MAS9.GLOBAL_PROPERTY_AND_LOCAL_COMPOSITION: Local compliance, availability and collective progress are checked separately; fault tolerance is scoped to a stated invariant.
MAS9.DYNAMIC_MEMBERSHIP_LEARNING_AND_NONSTATI: Admission, software changes and repaired participants can alter evidence and fault assumptions.
MAS9.FAILURE_DECEPTION_AND_COMMON_MODE_ASSUMP: Common-mode errors, colluding actors and abandoned obligations are not neutralised by naming more agents.
MAS9.COLLECTIVE_EVALUATION_AND_COORDINATION_C: Measure degradation and recovery cost, false suspicion and failure-layer bottlenecks; redundancy is justified against a specific threat.

MAS10.AGENT_POPULATION_AND_SYSTEM_BOUNDARY: Evaluated collectives may be software-only, LLM-based, human-agent or mixed; population and task sampling are explicit.
MAS10.GOAL_ALIGNMENT_AND_INCENTIVE_ASSUMPTIONS: An evaluation contract specifies useful outcomes, costs and unacceptable harms; benchmark score is not institutional approval.
MAS10.INFORMATION_AND_CONTROL_DISTRIBUTION: Baselines receive comparable information, tools and budgets; different access conditions must be reported rather than hidden.
MAS10.COMMUNICATION_AND_PROTOCOL_SEMANTICS: Trace review separates valid messages, consequential understanding and actual progress; shared prompts and models create evidence dependence.
MAS10.TASK_COMMITMENT_OR_RESOURCE_INTERDEPENDE: Coordination-specific outcomes must be separable from base-model competence and isolated task completion.
MAS10.ORGANISATIONAL_AUTHORITY_AND_NORMS: Humans retain whatever decision rights the external setting establishes; an evaluation does not transfer them to the system.
MAS10.GLOBAL_PROPERTY_AND_LOCAL_COMPOSITION: End-to-end outcomes and uncertainty qualify local or benchmark success; one programme does not provide independent replications.
MAS10.DYNAMIC_MEMBERSHIP_LEARNING_AND_NONSTATI: Changing models, prompts, partners and APIs require versioned evaluation; historical benchmarks do not certify later versions.
MAS10.FAILURE_DECEPTION_AND_COMMON_MODE_ASSUMP: Correlated judging, selected tasks, omitted failures and missing ground truth limit inference even from large trace collections.
MAS10.COLLECTIVE_EVALUATION_AND_COORDINATION_C: Compare matched reasoning, tool, latency and cost budgets and disclose unavoidable mismatches; include simpler non-agent alternatives.

COMPOSED.AGENT_POPULATION_AND_SYSTEM_BOUNDARY: The analytical system is a conditional configuration of actual decision participants, task objects, commitments, protocols and external interfaces.
COMPOSED.GOAL_ALIGNMENT_AND_INCENTIVE_ASSUMPTIONS: Cooperative, strategic, normative and learning branches retain different assumptions rather than being forced into one unanimous utility model.
COMPOSED.INFORMATION_AND_CONTROL_DISTRIBUTION: Each composition boundary identifies who may observe, decide and act; no omniscient central state is presumed.
COMPOSED.COMMUNICATION_AND_PROTOCOL_SEMANTICS: Communication couples local evidence to relevant consumers and actions; successful reporting is not successful operation.
COMPOSED.TASK_COMMITMENT_OR_RESOURCE_INTERDEPENDE: Relations connect tasks, commitments, resources, objectives and revision dependencies without requiring every candidate mechanism.
COMPOSED.ORGANISATIONAL_AUTHORITY_AND_NORMS: External principals and participants supply authority; the composed model grants no rights and cannot warrant its own adoption.
COMPOSED.GLOBAL_PROPERTY_AND_LOCAL_COMPOSITION: Whole-system properties arise from specific coupling and remain analytical until tested; constituent evidence alone does not validate the composition.
COMPOSED.DYNAMIC_MEMBERSHIP_LEARNING_AND_NONSTATI: Changed membership, incentive regime or policy invalidates dependent assumptions and triggers scoped reconsideration, not automatic global redesign.
COMPOSED.FAILURE_DECEPTION_AND_COMMON_MODE_ASSUMP: Observation gaps, incompatible guarantees and coordination-layer failures can defeat the entire composition despite locally correct parts.
COMPOSED.COLLECTIVE_EVALUATION_AND_COORDINATION_C: The minimum adequate configuration competes with simpler alternatives; total coordination cost and outstanding uncertainty remain visible.
